name: ChatGPT
best_for_usecase: General-purpose chat, writing, analysis and brainstorming for individuals and teams
hidden_limits: Free tier has message caps and lower-tier models; Plus still throttles heavy use of the newest models and image generation.
ai_model: OpenAI GPT-6 family (Instant and Reasoning models)
pros: Broadest feature set: voice, images, files, custom GPTs
Strong at writing, coding and analysis
cons: Usage caps even on paid plans
Team plans cost more per seat

name: Claude
best_for_usecase: Long-document analysis, careful writing and coding with large context windows
hidden_limits: Usage is metered in rolling windows; heavy users on Pro can hit message limits during peak hours.
pros: Projects and Artifacts for organized work
cons: Rate limits can interrupt long sessions

name: Google Gemini
best_for_usecase: Teams living in Google Workspace who want AI in Docs, Gmail and Drive
hidden_limits: Top-tier model access and Deep Research quotas are capped per day; Workspace AI features need a qualifying plan.
pros: Deep integration with Gmail, Docs and Drive
cons: Plan names and bundles change often
Privacy controls differ between consumer and Workspace

name: Perplexity
best_for_usecase: Cited, source-backed web research and fact-finding
hidden_limits: Free plan limits Pro searches per day; advanced model choice and file uploads need Pro.
ai_model: Sonar plus selectable GPT and Claude models
pros: Lets you pick between several frontier models
cons: Weaker for creative or long-form writing

name: Microsoft Copilot
best_for_usecase: Organizations on Microsoft 365 wanting AI inside Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams
hidden_limits: Microsoft 365 Copilot requires an eligible Microsoft 365 base license on top of the add-on fee, often with annual commitment.
ai_model: OpenAI GPT models via Microsoft Azure
pros: Works inside the Office apps you already use
Grounded in your tenant data via Microsoft Graph
cons: Value depends on how much you use Office

name: Ollama
best_for_usecase: Running open LLMs locally and privately on your own hardware
hidden_limits: Free to run, but model quality and speed depend entirely on your GPU, RAM and the open model you pick; no vendor support.
ai_model: Runs Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen and other open models locally
pros: Fully private: data never leaves your machine
Simple CLI and local API for developers
cons: Needs capable hardware for large models
Open models trail the best hosted ones

name: Midjourney
best_for_usecase: High-aesthetic concept art, brand imagery and stylized illustrations
hidden_limits: Basic plan includes only about 3.3 fast GPU hours per month; unlimited Relax mode starts at Standard and Stealth mode requires Pro.
pros: Strong style and character reference tools
cons: Images are public unless you pay for Stealth
Less precise text rendering and layout control

name: Runway
best_for_usecase: AI video generation and editing for creators and marketing teams
hidden_limits: Everything is credit-based; video generation burns credits per second so the monthly allowance can run out in a few clips.
pros: Editing tools like inpainting and motion brush
cons: Free plan is a one-time credit grant
Output length per clip is short

name: ElevenLabs
best_for_usecase: Realistic text-to-speech, voiceovers and voice cloning
hidden_limits: Plans are credit-based by character; commercial licensing starts at the Starter tier and professional voice cloning needs higher plans.
ai_model: Eleven Multilingual v2 and Eleven v3
pros: Very natural-sounding voices in many languages
cons: Free plan has no commercial license
Credits run out on long-form audio

name: Leonardo.ai
best_for_usecase: Game assets, product visuals and consistent image styles with fine control
hidden_limits: Daily or monthly token allowance governs generations; private generations and faster queues need paid tiers.
ai_model: Leonardo Phoenix and Lucid models, plus Flux
pros: Fine-grained controls and custom model training
cons: Token system takes time to understand

name: Jasper
best_for_usecase: On-brand marketing copy at scale for content and growth teams
hidden_limits: No permanent free plan (trial only); brand voice, knowledge base and collaboration features are gated to higher tiers.
pros: Brand voice and style guide memory
cons: Overlaps with what ChatGPT or Claude can do

name: Grammarly
best_for_usecase: Real-time grammar, tone and clarity fixes across every app you write in
hidden_limits: Free tier covers basic spelling and grammar only; AI generation prompts are capped monthly and advanced tone/plagiarism checks need Pro.
pros: Works in browser, desktop and mobile apps
Team style guides on business plans
cons: Browser extension can slow heavy editors

name: Copy.ai
best_for_usecase: Go-to-market copy workflows and repeatable sales and marketing automations
hidden_limits: Plans bundle a fixed number of seats and workflow credits; extra seats and higher workflow volume cost more.
pros: Workflow builder for repeatable GTM tasks
cons: Product focus has shifted toward enterprise GTM

name: GitHub Copilot
best_for_usecase: Inline code completion and chat inside VS Code, JetBrains and GitHub
hidden_limits: Free plan has monthly completion and chat caps; premium model requests are metered and extra requests are billed on paid plans.
ai_model: Selectable GPT, Claude and Gemini models
pros: Works in the editors developers already use
Deep GitHub integration for PRs and issues

name: Cursor
best_for_usecase: AI-first code editor for multi-file edits and agent-driven development
hidden_limits: Pro includes a usage allowance for premium models; heavy agent use can exhaust it and require Ultra or usage-based billing.
ai_model: Claude, GPT and Gemini plus Cursor in-house models
pros: Strong codebase-aware editing and agent mode
cons: Usage limits can surprise heavy users
Pricing model has changed several times
Not a plugin: requires switching editors

name: Replit
best_for_usecase: Building and deploying apps from a prompt entirely in the browser
hidden_limits: Agent runs, compute and deployments consume credits beyond the monthly allowance; heavy app usage can add usage-based charges.
ai_model: Replit Agent (powered by Claude and other LLMs)
cons: Costs can climb with agent usage
Less control than a local toolchain

name: Windsurf
best_for_usecase: Agentic AI IDE with fast flow-based coding assistance
hidden_limits: Monthly prompt credits are capped; premium models consume more credits and extra credits are purchased separately.
ai_model: SWE-1 plus Claude and GPT models
pros: Capable agent that edits across files
cons: Ownership and roadmap have shifted recently

name: Asana
best_for_usecase: Cross-functional teams that need structured projects, timelines and goals
hidden_limits: Free plan caps at 10 users; timelines, portfolios and advanced reporting require higher tiers, and annual billing is cheaper than monthly.
pros: Polished list, board and timeline views
cons: Can get expensive as seats grow
Best features sit on higher tiers

name: Trello
best_for_usecase: Simple kanban boards for small teams and personal workflows
hidden_limits: Free workspaces limit boards and automation runs; calendar and timeline views need Premium.
cons: Not built for complex multi-project planning

name: ClickUp
best_for_usecase: Teams wanting tasks, docs and goals in one highly customizable workspace
hidden_limits: Free plan limits storage and uses; ClickUp Brain AI is a paid add-on per user on top of the plan price.
pros: Docs, whiteboards and chat in one app
cons: Performance can lag on big workspaces

name: Monday.com
best_for_usecase: Visual work management for operations, marketing and sales teams
hidden_limits: Paid plans require a minimum of 3 seats; automations, integrations and dashboards are capped per tier.

name: Linear
best_for_usecase: Fast, opinionated issue tracking and sprint planning for software teams
hidden_limits: Free plan is limited to a small number of issues and teams; advanced insights, SLAs and unlimited history need higher plans.
pros: Clean cycles, roadmaps and GitHub sync
cons: Built for software teams, less for general work
Paid tiers add up for large teams

name: Jira
best_for_usecase: Agile software teams needing configurable workflows, scrum and kanban
hidden_limits: Free plan is limited to 10 users; advanced roadmaps, audit logs and automation volume depend on the tier.
cons: Can be overkill for small teams

name: Plane
best_for_usecase: Open-source Jira alternative you can self-host or use in the cloud
hidden_limits: Self-hosted Community edition is free; hosted Pro and enterprise features (SSO, advanced analytics) are paid and may differ from the open core.
ai_model: Plane AI (LLM-powered, bring-your-own key on self-host)
cons: Some features reserved for paid editions

name: HubSpot
best_for_usecase: Growing teams unifying CRM, marketing and sales automation
hidden_limits: Free CRM is generous but caps marketing contacts and emails; costs rise sharply when you add Professional hubs or onboarding fees.
cons: Required onboarding fees on higher plans

name: Salesforce
best_for_usecase: Enterprise sales organizations needing a customizable CRM platform
hidden_limits: Entry-level Starter Suite is limited; customization, automation and storage need higher editions, plus implementation and admin costs.

name: Pipedrive
best_for_usecase: Small sales teams that want a visual, pipeline-first CRM
hidden_limits: The lowest tier has limited automation and reporting; the quoted price assumes annual billing and add-ons like LeadBooster cost extra.

name: Zoho CRM
best_for_usecase: Budget-conscious businesses wanting broad CRM features and the Zoho suite
hidden_limits: Free edition is limited to a handful of users; workflow rules, custom modules and API calls scale with plan tier.
pros: Strong value across the Zoho ecosystem
cons: Integrations outside Zoho are less polished

name: Twenty
best_for_usecase: Teams wanting an open-source, customizable CRM they can self-host
hidden_limits: Self-hosting is free but you manage infra and updates; hosted cloud pricing and some enterprise features are paid.
pros: Open source (AGPL) with full data ownership

name: Figma
best_for_usecase: Collaborative UI/UX design, prototyping and design systems
hidden_limits: Free Starter limits files and editing seats; Dev Mode and advanced libraries need paid seat types, and seat types are billed separately.
ai_model: Figma AI (Make and design assist features)

name: Canva
best_for_usecase: Non-designers creating social posts, presentations and marketing assets quickly
hidden_limits: Premium templates, Brand Kit and Magic Studio AI credits are limited on free and capped on Pro; Teams needs a minimum of 3 seats.
ai_model: Canva Magic Studio (Magic Design, Magic Write)
cons: Less precise than pro design tools

name: Penpot
best_for_usecase: Open-source design and prototyping with design-code collaboration
hidden_limits: The core app is free and self-hostable; hosted paid plans add storage, history and admin features and may change.
pros: Uses open standards like SVG, CSS grid and flex
Free for individuals and small teams

name: Framer
best_for_usecase: Designing and publishing polished marketing sites without code
hidden_limits: Pricing is per published site and tied to page, CMS and bandwidth limits; collaborators on a team are billed separately.
pros: Design and publish in one tool
Built-in hosting, CMS and SEO controls

name: Notion
best_for_usecase: All-in-one docs, wikis and lightweight project tracking for teams
hidden_limits: Free plan limits block history and guests; the full Notion AI features moved into higher tiers, so the cheapest paid plan may not include them.
pros: Flexible docs, databases and wikis in one place
cons: Can get slow on large workspaces
AI features gated to higher tiers

name: Airtable
best_for_usecase: Relational databases with views, forms and automations for ops teams
hidden_limits: Strict record limits per base (1,000 on Free, 50,000 on Team); automation runs and sync features are capped per plan.
pros: Great views: grid, kanban, gallery, calendar

name: Obsidian
best_for_usecase: Private, local-first note-taking and personal knowledge graphs
hidden_limits: The app is free; Sync and Publish are optional paid add-ons, and there is no built-in real-time team collaboration.
pros: Notes are plain Markdown files you own

name: Coda
best_for_usecase: Interactive docs that blend text, tables and automations into mini apps
hidden_limits: Free plan limits doc size and automation runs; only Doc Makers are billed, but editors and viewers have capped permissions.
pros: Only makers are billed on many plans

name: Slack
best_for_usecase: Real-time team messaging with deep app integrations
hidden_limits: Free workspaces keep only 90 days of message history and limit integrations; Slack AI is only available on higher tiers.
cons: Price rises with the AI tier

name: Zoom
best_for_usecase: Reliable video meetings and webinars for teams and clients
hidden_limits: Free meetings are capped at 40 minutes; phone, large-meeting and webinar add-ons are billed separately.
pros: AI Companion included on paid plans
Easy for external guests to join
cons: Feature overlap with Teams and Meet

name: Loom
best_for_usecase: Async video updates, walkthroughs and product demos
hidden_limits: Free Starter plan caps videos at 25 per person and 5 minutes each; AI features and unlimited recording need Business.
pros: Fastest way to record and share a video
cons: Storage and branding tied to tiers

name: Zapier
best_for_usecase: No-code automation between thousands of apps
hidden_limits: Pricing is by monthly task count; multi-step Zaps, premium apps and higher task volumes require paid tiers and overages are charged.
cons: Costs more than Make or n8n at volume

name: Make
best_for_usecase: Visual, multi-branch automation scenarios at lower per-operation cost
hidden_limits: Plans are metered by operations; each module run counts, so complex scenarios can burn through the monthly allowance.
ai_model: Make AI Agents (bring your own model)
cons: Operation counting is easy to misjudge

name: n8n
best_for_usecase: Technical teams building self-hostable workflow and AI-agent automations
hidden_limits: Source-available under the Sustainable Use License (not OSI open source); cloud plans are limited by monthly executions and self-hosting is free for internal use only.
ai_model: AI nodes for OpenAI, Anthropic and local LLMs

name: Mailchimp
best_for_usecase: Email newsletters and simple marketing automation for small businesses
hidden_limits: Price scales with contact count and the free plan has tight send limits and no automation beyond basics; unsubscribed contacts can still count.
pros: Handy audience tools and landing pages
cons: Costs climb as your list grows
Reporting and segmentation lag niche rivals

name: Semrush
best_for_usecase: SEO, keyword research and competitor analysis for marketing teams
hidden_limits: Pro plan limits tracked projects, keywords and daily reports; extra users, Local and the AI Toolkit are billed as add-ons.

name: Buffer
best_for_usecase: Simple social media scheduling and publishing for creators and small brands
hidden_limits: Pricing is per connected channel; free plan allows only 3 channels and a limited post queue.
cons: Analytics are basic on lower tiers

name: PostHog
best_for_usecase: Product analytics, session replay and feature flags in one open-source suite
hidden_limits: Usage-based billing with a generous free monthly allowance; costs scale with events, recordings and flag requests beyond free quotas.
pros: Generous free tier and no per-seat fees
cons: Usage costs can spike at scale

name: Plausible
best_for_usecase: Lightweight, privacy-first website analytics without cookie banners
hidden_limits: Cloud pricing scales by monthly pageviews; the self-hosted Community Edition is free but lacks some cloud features.

name: Intercom
best_for_usecase: Conversational support, in-app messaging and an AI agent for SaaS companies
hidden_limits: The Fin AI agent is billed per resolution on top of seat fees, and advanced features sit on much pricier tiers.
ai_model: Fin AI Agent (OpenAI and Anthropic models)
pros: Fin AI resolves many tickets automatically

name: Zendesk
best_for_usecase: Scalable ticketing, help centers and omnichannel support operations
hidden_limits: Entry tier is email and basic ticketing only; messaging, automation, AI agents and advanced analytics require higher plans or add-ons.
